newsitem.title: ROMANIA: Romania March monthly inflation record high.
newsitem.headline: Romania March monthly inflation record high.

text.p: Monthly inflation in Romania hit a record 30.7 percent in March, up from 18.8 percent in Feburary, and officials blamed the continued effects of price liberalisation under market reforms.

The National Statistics Board said the increase pushed inflation for the first quarter to 76.5 percent. The year-on-year rise for March stood at 164.0 percent. The central bank (BNR) earlier this week forecast a rise of between 10 and 12 percent for March. A BNR spokesman said that figure had referred only to underlying price rises and did not include adjustments after price liberalisation.

"The government reform programme went into force in February and price adjustments started immediately" BNR spokesman Adrian Vasilescu said. "The adjustments to telephone, transport and fuel prices had their effects on the March figure."

Wednesday's figure was an all-time high for any single month since prices were first freed in October 1990, less than a year after the fall of communist rule. February's figure of 18.8 percent was a record over 45 months.
Under the reform programme and the 1997 budget, to be presented to parliament on Thursday, monthly inflation is to fall to 2.2 percent by the end of the year.
Romania's centrist government signed a letter of intent on Wednesday to restore International Monetary Fund credits suspended last year.

The IMF chief negotiator said the budget and its provisions were a key part to resuming the credits. The IMF is to examine the letter, believed to call for credits of about $400 million, at a board meeting later this month.
